## Learning goals of today

-   Selecting a good research project
-   Finding data for research project
-   Starting the project in R

# Selecting research project

## Why a research project

-   Intrinsic motivation pivotal
-   Many courses teach some R, but...
-   Passive learning less effective
-   Active learning by doing improves learning outcomes

## Learning by doing

-   Learning by doing is how most people learn R
-   I want to guide you through the process
-   Empowering you to continue learning

## Good research projects

-   Aim for a SMART project

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
-   **S** pecific
-   **M** easurable
-   **A** chievable
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
-   **R** elevant
-   **T** imely
:::
:::::

## Specific

-   Less specific: Has population growth increased?
-   More specific: Has population growth across countries increased the past 10 years?

## Measurable

-   Less measurable: How has sentiment on inflation changed?
-   More measurable: How have people's responses to inflation questions in standard surveys changed over time?

## Achievable

-   Less achievable: How have consumption patterns of Germans versus non-Germans changed over the past 40 years using G-SOEP data?
-   More achievable: What are consumption patterns of Germans versus non-Germans using G-SOEP data?

## Relevant

-   Less relevant: How often do people in Germany use their car?
-   More relevant: How has car use changed in light of the recent increases in fuel costs due to the war on Iran?

## Timely

-   Less timely: How has the Spanish flue pandemic from 1918-20 changed population at local levels using historical data?
-   More timely: How has the Covid-19 pandemic affected population across the ages using UN population estimates?

# Where to find data

## Types of data

-   There are many types of data
-   For our purposes two types are the most interesting:
    -   Survey data
    -   Administrative data

## Survey data

-   Survey data are set of questions asked to a sample of a population

-   Ideally random selection allows for inference of population parameters using sample estimates

-   Very expensive if done well

## Survey data: Pros and Cons

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**PRO**

-   Include wide array of questions
-   Representative of a population
-   Sometimes comparable, sometimes panels
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**CONTRA**

-   Can be quite complex
-   Often more difficult to gain access
:::
:::::

## Survey data: Examples

-   These are some potential surveys you can use:

-   European Social Survey: <https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/>

-   World Value Survey: <https://www.worldvaluessurvey.org/>

-   For a range of surveys (in Germany) check out GESIS: <https://www.gesis.org/angebot/daten-finden-und-abrufen/ueberblick>

## Administrative data

-   Administrative data is data that is collected by governments regularly

-   Huge range of potentially relevant data sets

-   Data often collected more consistently (in Global North)

-   Be careful of changes in definition of underlying properties (!)

## Administrative data: Pros and Cons

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**PRO**

-   Often large amounts of data (in rich countries)
-   Contains information relevant for governments
-   Often less complex and simpler analysis
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**CONTRA**

-   Often requires more data wrangling to combine
-   May have data gaps or breaks in temporal data
:::
:::::

## Administrative data: Examples

-   These are many sources of administrative data

-   I would recommend reliable sources from established institutions:

-   UN population estimates: <https://population.un.org/wpp/>

-   World Bank: <https://data.worldbank.org/>

-   OECD: <https://www.oecd.org/en/data/datasets.html?orderBy=mostRelevant&page=0&facetTags=oecd-languages%3Aen>

## Administrative data: Access through API

-   Many administrative data sets are accessible without having to download them

-   Usually access happening through APIs (Application Programming Interface)

-   In effect, people write R-packages that allow one to access data sets directly from R

-   Example: <https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/data-science/world-bank-dataset-in-r/>

# Quarto project

## Why a "project"

-   Projects are self-containing environments for us to work in

-   Idea is that everything you need to work on your project is in one place

-   The project becomes (more) independent from the environment it is executed in

-   Enhances portability to other machines (your own or others)

## Starting new project

-   Create a new project in top-left corner of RStudio

-   We want to create new Quarto project

-   I will demonstrate in RStudio

## File system

-   File system is essential for reliable research

-   You should have one working directory with all files used in or created by project

-   Only exception could be data files due to their size

-   Makes sure that research is reproducible

## Reproducibility

-   Reproducibility is a lofty word but matters a lot for (quantitative) science

-   If your way of doing things changes the results of your calculations each time you do it that is very bad

-   Reproducibility and transparency also (!!!) for your future self

## Quick excursion: Referring to files

-   Way to refer to your files on your machine may depend on operating system used

    -   Main difference is using \\ versus / in paths

-   In Windows, most files are stored on C:\\

-   File location can be copied from top bar in Windows Explorer

    -   Just make sure to use the correct  or /

-   Use clearly identifiable folder names, such as \\data or \\output

## File types

-   Input files (such as data)

-   R- or Quarto-scripts that do the actual computation and transformation

-   Output files (such as PDF, HTML, PNG etc.)

## Script header

-   Each script you use should have a header with the most important information

-   Name of file and purpose of script

-   Data used

-   Author name and contact

-   Data created

-   Notes

## Example header

```{r}
#| echo: True

#--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Name: Data preparation
# Purpose: Preparation of OAA2 data analysis
# Data: OAA2 data, collected the in May and June 2024
# Author: Heiner Salomon (heiner.salomon@uni-bremen.de)
# Date created: 12/05/24
#
# Notes  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Preparation ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

```

## In Quarto: YAML header

-   Metadata of your Quarto file

-   starts and ends with - - -

-   Possible content:

    -   title: New project

    -   format: pdf

    -   author: Peter Peterson

    -   ...

-   For great overview, see: <https://charlotte.quarto.pub/cascadia/2-yaml-markdown-basics/2-yaml-markdown-basics.html#/title-slide>

-   For more details, see here: <https://quarto-tdg.org/yaml>
